calls.reason: The PDM and ECI papers guarantee restricted mathematical constraints. They neither establish broad physics or truthfulness guarantees nor show those guarantees are impossible.

Mashable reports disappearing objects and unnatural movement, and OpenAI acknowledges physics errors. But Marcus frames this as a tentative observation, which falls under the rule for hedged language.
Kang and colleagues find scaling limits in research models; OpenAI reports Sora 2 improvements. Neither isolates additional Sora training data sufficiently to call the forecast.
StEvo-Bench finds continuing Sora 2 Pro failures, while OpenAI reports physical improvements. These results do not settle whether future Sora versions can reliably understand physics.

Kang and colleagues report both successful learning and failures on unfamiliar situations. Sora's system card describes text-assisted training, leaving the broader claim about sensory learning unclear.
StEvo-Bench documents coherence failures alongside successes in models including Sora 2 Pro. Its broader coherence test cannot settle the claim that Sora will never grasp object permanence.
